prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies distribution circuits via transformer and feeder bays. The automation boundary covers bay-level monitoring/control, station coordination, and interfaces to external personnel and systems. Primary equipment, protection functions and field wiring stay under their approved designs and limits.

Elements:
- Bay Automation Controller (codename Juniper): performs bay sequencing, status evaluation and control permissive checks. Produces the Bay Status Digest for operational awareness. Requests breaker operations from the Breaker Control Unit only when the operating mode and permissives allow.
- North Bay Controller and South Bay Controller: provide bay-specific automation for their respective station portions.
- Feeder Protection Relay: detects feeder faults and initiates protection actions within its zone. Produces the Relay Diagnostic Note when self-monitoring finds a condition needing engineering attention.
- Breaker Control Unit: executes authorized breaker operations and enforces local electrical and mechanical interlocks.
- Station Supervisory Control System: station-level operating interface and supervisory coordination.
- Station Gateway: communications boundary for authorized external connections.
- Satellite Time Receiver: provides the time synchronization reference.
- Sequence Event Archive: retains operational event information.
- Engineering Workstation: authorized configuration and maintenance under controlled access.
- Maintenance Remote Terminal: approved maintenance access only; does not replace local operating authority.
- Station DC System: supplies control power to automation and protection equipment within its design capacity.

Actors:
- Control Room Operator: directs routine operation and verifies commanded states.
- Protection Relay Engineer: maintains protection settings and evaluates relay performance via the approved change process.
- Substation Field Crew: performs field checks and equipment work under switching instructions and clearances.

Modes/requirements:
- Local vs remote operation: local control takes precedence when equipment is selected for local operation.
- Remote commands are subject to station authority, bay selection, interlocking and equipment availability.
- Protection trips remain independent of routine bay-control commands, so a control failure cannot inhibit fault clearing.
- The supervisory architecture separates station-wide observation from local bay and protection functions.

New part:
S026: The Station Supervisory Control System is named Glasswing in this document.
S027: The Station Supervisory Control System presents available station and bay indications through a consolidated operator interface.
S028: Its displays show operating conditions and communication quality without replacing local equipment indications.
S029: The Station Gateway carries supervisory communications between station-level functions and remote operations interfaces.
S030: Supervisory visibility depends on the availability and quality of the underlying communications and status inputs.
S031: The supervisory layer does not perform the protective functions assigned to dedicated protection equipment.
S032: The Control Room Operator uses the supervisory displays to assess station conditions and coordinate operating actions.
S033: Any supervisory command remains subject to configured permissions and the applicable operating procedure.
S034: Local interlocks and equipment-level control logic remain authoritative for permitted switching actions.
S035: A communications interruption can leave displayed information stale or temporarily unavailable.
S036: After communications recover, operators confirm that indications are current before relying on them for decisions.
S037: The Satellite Time Receiver is named Bluefin in this document.
S038: The Satellite Time Receiver acquires a reference from supported satellite timing signals.
S039: It distributes time to station equipment over the configured time-distribution network.
S040: Time distribution supports consistent event timestamps across equipment that receives and applies the reference.
S041: Accurate timestamps assist event correlation but do not establish the validity of an electrical measurement or protection decision.
S042: If the external timing reference is lost, equipment behavior depends on its individual clock and holdover capabilities.
S043: Holdover performance varies by device and may degrade as the interval without a valid reference increases.
S044: The Satellite Time Receiver produces the Clock Drift Snapshot when its measured offset meets the configured reporting condition.
S045: Time-quality indications allow operators to distinguish synchronized operation from degraded or unavailable timing.
S046: The Station DC System supplies operating power to station automation equipment within its designed capacity.
S047: A loss of station power can interrupt supervisory visibility and time distribution until supported supplies are restored.
S048: The Station Supervisory Control System produces the Alarm Acknowledgement Slip for supervisory recordkeeping.
S049: The Substation Supervisor oversees operational use of the supervisory system and escalation of unresolved availability concerns.
S050: The Feeder Protection Relay is known as Tandem in this concept.
S051: The Protection Relay Engineer is known as Larkspur in this concept.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
